messages.subject: Random intercept prior error
parts:
Hello,
I'm trying to fit logistic regression with 1 fixed effect and random intercept. When I don't specify prior for random intercept precision, the fitted precision is enormously high. I read here that it could help specify priors, so I chose gamma(0.5, 0.02), but the program crashes.

Here is the code:

formula <- y ~ x + f(subject, model = "iid", hyper = list(prec = list(prior = "gamma", param = c(0.5, 0.02))))

inla_fit <- inla(
  formula,
  family = "binomial",
  data = simulated_data,
  control.predictor = list(link = 1)
)

And here is the error I get:

*** inla.core.safe: The inla program failed, but will rerun in case better initial values may help. try=1/1 Error in inla.core.safe(formula = formula, family = family, contrasts = contrasts, : The inla program call crashed. The inla program failed and the maximum number of tries has been reached.

My versions of R, INLA and other packages are installed newly 2 days ago. I also tried around 20 other Gamma settings, but found only one that works - Gamma(1, 0.1). Is it commot to not be able to choose hyperarameters for priors or am I not seeing something clearly?

Thanks!

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Random intercept prior error
parts:
Hi,
Not entirely clear without info about the data size etc if this is the reason, but your model actually has _two_ fixed effects, as R’s formula system adds an automatic intercept terms unless you tell it not to do that. You can remove that with e.g.
  Y~ 0+ x+…
In the formula specification.

But also, if the data doesn’t need the subject level iid effect, due to the variability being sufficiently explained by the common intercept and x-covariate effect and the inherent binomial variability, then that can explain why it estimates a large precision.
Since your model has binary data, this can easily happen if the data size is small.

Finn
